segments.text: This is my DIY RC sim-racing controller build: a receiver adapter, a little firmware, a custom case, and a track test.
The core is a receiver adapter that reads two RC channels and presents itself to the PC as a USB joystick.
Its firmware is tiny: throttle on pin two, steering on pin three, mapped straight onto the joystick axes.
The adapter needed a home, so I modelled a case in 3table, the CAD editor I built myself.
Starting from a blank grid, I shaped a long grey shell around the circuit board — a green lid, snap-fit tabs, and a power switch up front.
Inside there are ribs, threaded mounting posts, and slots that hold the board exactly where it needs to sit.
Full disclosure: I was filming with one hand and steering with the other, so the driving is, frankly, brave.
But the controller worked, and that is the whole point.
Receiver adapter, a few lines of firmware, a case modelled in 3table, and one very sketchy lap. Thanks for watching.
